In detail

Sussex Police recorded 385 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 7.6 per 1,000 residents, the 12th highest rate of Brighton and Hove's 21 wards. The daytime score here is driven by drugs (5), vehicle crime (4), shoplifting (2); the evening/night score by violent crime (57), anti social behaviour (29), public order (10). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Moulsecoomb and Bevendean safe?

Wandroz currently rates Moulsecoomb and Bevendean in Brighton and Hove as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove at night. This rating is derived from Sussex Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Moulsecoomb and Bevendean safe at night?

At night, Moulsecoomb and Bevendean is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Moulsecoomb and Bevendean a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Moulsecoomb and Bevendean's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Brighton and Hove) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
